## What a bundle contains

A run of `sas_translate()` leaves the translated programs at the top of its run folder,
next to a few files they depend on:

```
run_20260907T120000Z_1a2b3c4d/
├── adsl.R                 <- translated programs
├── adae.R
├── autoexec.R             <- the library paths; every program sources it first
├── sas2r-helpers.R        <- the runtime: the functions the programs call
├── _sas2r_formats.R       <- the compiled format catalog
└── report.md
```

The programs run **without sas2r installed**. Each opens with a short bootstrap block that
finds `autoexec.R` -- in the nearest directory at or above the program -- and sources it into
the program's own environment. `autoexec.R` is the bundle's counterpart of a SAS autoexec:
generated by the translation, and yours to maintain afterwards. Its LIBRARIES section is the
list of librefs and where each reads from and writes to; its LOAD section loads the helpers
and the formats. The runtime the bundle carries is the package's own runtime: `sas2r-helpers.R` is rendered from the same
source files that define `lib_read()`, `sas_sort()` and the rest inside sas2r, and a test
fails if the two ever differ. A bundle still always loads its own copy, so what it does never
depends on which sas2r is installed.

## Running a program

Programs run the way SAS programs do: from their folder, with their autoexec. Each program
opens with one guarded line, `source("autoexec.R", chdir = TRUE)`, and any of these works:

```bash
cd run_20260907T120000Z_1a2b3c4d && Rscript adsl.R     # batch
```

<!-- sas2r-example: offline runtime-1 -->
```r
setwd("run_20260907T120000Z_1a2b3c4d")     # or open the run folder as the working directory
source("adsl.R")
```

<!-- sas2r-example: offline runtime-2 -->
```r
source("run_20260907T120000Z_1a2b3c4d/autoexec.R", chdir = TRUE)   # once per session ...
source("run_20260907T120000Z_1a2b3c4d/adsl.R")                     # ... then any program, from anywhere
```

A program run from some other working directory before the autoexec has run fails on that
first line, because `autoexec.R` is not there. Pasted code works after the autoexec has run.

## Maintaining `autoexec.R`

Open it when data moves. The LIBRARIES section reads like this:

<!-- sas2r-example: offline runtime-3 -->
```r
.sas2r_registry <- list(
  adam = list(read_path = "/study/data/adam", write_path = "adam", engine = "sas7bdat", write = "rds"),
  work = list(read_path = "work",             write_path = "work", engine = "rds",      write = "rds")
)
```

A relative path means *inside this folder*; an absolute path is used as is. So a run folder can
be moved or renamed **as a whole** -- the session `work` library and every library the programs
write travel with it -- and only the source data the programs read, recorded absolutely, needs
an edit when it moves. A commented `<FILL>` entry is a library some program reads and nothing
binds: set its path and uncomment it. A `LIBNAME` inside a program still binds its libref where
it stands, exactly as in SAS, so `autoexec.R` is the seed. Nothing under LOAD needs editing. A
single program moved out of its folder stops with a message, because its runtime stayed behind.

## Using the runtime interactively

Source `autoexec.R` once per session, with `chdir = TRUE` so its own folder is the working
directory while it loads -- the R counterpart of running a SAS autoexec. It loads the library
paths, the helpers, and the formats into your session, and every program's header then finds
the runtime already loaded and skips its own bootstrap:

<!-- sas2r-example: offline runtime-4 -->
```r
bundle <- "run_20260907T120000Z_1a2b3c4d"
source(file.path(bundle, "autoexec.R"), chdir = TRUE)   # paths, helpers, formats, once

adsl <- lib_read("adam", "adsl")     # honours the registry's paths and formats
adsl$USUBJID                         # column names resolve case-insensitively
sas_sort(adsl, by = "usubjid")
```

The helpers `autoexec.R` loads are the bundle's own copy, which is the same code sas2r
exports, so this works with or without sas2r installed; attach the package (`library(sas2r)`)
when you want the help pages.

Two rules the data-access helpers enforce, because a wrong call in a translated program should
fail loudly rather than be reinterpreted: `lib_read()` takes the libref and member as two
separate strings, and `lib_write()` takes the data frame first --
`lib_write(df, "adam", "adsl")`. Combined `"lib.member"` strings and single-argument calls are
rejected with the canonical form in the message.

## The reference

The full reference is the help topic:

<!-- sas2r-example: offline runtime-5 -->
```r
library(sas2r)
?sas2r_runtime      # the overview, grouped
?lib_read           # each exported helper has its own page and examples
```

In brief, the runtime covers:

| Group | Helpers |
|---|---|
| Data access | `lib_read()`, `lib_write()`, `sas2r_libname_assign()`, `sas2r_libname_clear()`, `sas2r_fold_names()`, the `sas2r_dataset` `$`/`[[` methods |
| SAS value semantics | `chr_cmp()`, `%notin%`, `%+%`, `sas_if_else()`, `sas_sum()`, `sas_mean()`, `sas_min()`, `sas_max()`, `sas_round()`, `sas_length()`, `sas_substr()`, `sas_compress()`, `sas_display()` |
| Sorting and merging | `sas_sort()`, `sas_merge()` |
| Formats | `apply_format()`, `sas_put()` |
| Includes | `sas2r_source_include()` |
| Internal (generated code only, not exported) | `sas2r_registry_env()`, `sas2r_lib_entry()`, `sas2r_lib_member_path()`, `sas2r_libref_stop()`, `split_ds()` |

Every one of them reproduces a SAS behavior R does not share by default: missing values sort
low and compare the SAS way, trailing blanks are cosmetic, rounding is half away from zero,
`SUM()` and `MEAN()` are row-wise, `MERGE` follows SAS's overlap and `IN=` rules.

## Versioning and stability

The first line of every vendored `sas2r-helpers.R` states which sas2r version generated it:

```
# sas2r runtime helpers -- vendored by sas2r 0.2.0. Do not edit by hand.
```

A bundle is frozen on purpose. It always loads its own copy of the runtime, so what a
validated bundle does depends only on its own contents -- never on which sas2r is installed,
and never on an upgrade. Fixes to the runtime reach a bundle when it is translated again.

The promise behind that:

- Within a major version, an existing helper never changes what it does for the same inputs.
- A helper is retired only after a replacement ships and the old name has warned for at least
  one minor version.
- The lint allowlist, the help topic, and the runtime file are held in sync by the package's
  tests, so a helper cannot be added or removed in one place only.

## Where this is going

The runtime is now an exported, versioned source of truth inside sas2r, vendored into bundles
from that source. When usage justifies it, it becomes a separate `sas2r.runtime` package that
organizations can validate once, with an opt-in mode that writes `library(sas2r.runtime)` into
bundles. The decision and its phases are recorded in the repository at
`docs/decisions/0003-runtime-helpers-distribution.md`.
